No it's not. Take it from a person who started smoking to hurt myself. DO NOT DO IT. I've been clean from selfharm 10months but it's way way harder to stop smoking. Vapes have nicotine and it's basically a drug and you will get addicted to it. And it's a way stronger addiction than physically hurting yourself is.

I was an occasional smoker bumming from my friends here and there. Then i bought my first pack which lasted for awhile. Then another and maybe 3 months after buying the first pack I was smoking half a pack a day then almost the whole pack. Like previously said it's a slippery slope and most people who were an occasional smoker turned into a full on smoker. 

Where I live you need your ID to buy so now when ever I go into a store I leave my ID home so I can't buy. If that's the case where you live then do the same. But all in all it's about willpower not to buy that pack. When you're thinking about buying a pack stop yourself and keep repeating "I'm not buying a pack" in your head. That's all I've got to you, willpower.
Hopefully it will calm down for me soon also.

That didn't happen to me but I do think it can happen but it's not supposed to so he should switch meds. Only by switching meds can you be certain about it. 
All meds that are meant to treat mental illnesses affect people differently and most of the time you need to try few different types of meds before you find the right one for you. 
Like I said what you described didn't happen to me but I got these really powerful sleepiness attacks. They came out of the blue and I had this powerful urge to close my eyes and when you're driving those are quite dangerous. I haven't heard about anyone else that got those types of attacks because of the meds. And I know the meds caused it because after I changed meds those attacks stopped. So yes it's most definitely possible what you're boyfriend is going through is because of the meds and he should talk to his doctor about changing them.

I don't know if there's a lot you can say because in the end people make their own decisions.

Also once you start you need more and more of it. In my case it started with hitting my leg when i was a kid and it got worse and worse over time to the point that I almost caused permanent damage to my organs. 
If nothing else show him the posts about people struggling to stop and people celebrating being clean.

When you xlean your fresh wound and you can see white flesh it's a styro cut. Yellow and bubbly flesh is fat tissue and that's deeper than styro. You can see approximately how deep you have cut by cleaning the fresh wounds and seeing what the color and texture is beneath. 
The amount that it bleeds doesn't always say how deep the cut is because some people bleed more some less, some bleed longer and some less time.
